data.title: Slavic hillforts in the Orava region – Ostrá skala and others
data.excerpt: Ostrá skala above Vyšný Kubín is one of the most thoroughly investigated sites in the Orava region: occupied from the Eneolithic onwards, refortified by the Slavs at the turn of the 8th and 9th centuries and surviving until the 12th century, when it probably still served as an administrative seat. Alongside it, the article surveys the sites at Dolný Kubín, Istebné and Oravský Podzámok, the Orava group of the Lusatian cultural complex and the Hallstatt hillfort at Sedliacka Dubová.
data.metaTitle: Slavic hillforts in the Orava region – Ostrá skala
data.metaDescription: Hillforts in the Orava region such as Ostrá skala above Vyšný Kubín were occupied from the Eneolithic and reused by the Slavs in the Early Middle Ages.

keyFacts.label: Vyšný Kubín — Ostrá skala
keyFacts.value: The most thoroughly investigated site in the Orava region (812 m a.s.l.), occupied from the Eneolithic; a fortification with three enclosures covering 1.5–2 ha

keyFacts.label: Dolný Kubín — Veľký Bysterec-Trniny
keyFacts.value: An upland site with finds of Carolingian mounts; a Slavic fortification can so far be considered only in theoretical terms

keyFacts.label: Istebné — Hrádok
keyFacts.value: A promontory above the Orava river, a Hallstatt hillfort reused in the Early Middle Ages; part of it destroyed by the construction of the railway (1898)

keyFacts.label: Oravský Podzámok — Hrad
keyFacts.value: A 9th-century upland settlement on the spot where Orava Castle has stood since the 13th century

keyFacts.label: The hillfort at Dubová
keyFacts.value: A Hallstatt hillfort with a 6 m high neck rampart, a supporting stone wall, a defensive gallery and a gate tower with a bridge

keyFacts.label: The Orava group
keyFacts.value: A local group of the Lusatian cultural complex with its own pottery and bronzes, in close contact with neighbouring Poland

timeline.title: The Orava group of the Lusatian cultural complex
timeline.description: A local group occupying the northern basin of the Váh, the Orava and the Turiec; relevantly attested from 550 BC (Ha D2) onwards, with a dense network of hillforts and hamlets.

timeline.title: A system of upland hillforts
timeline.description: Fortified settlements at Tvrdošín, Podbiel, Istebné, Vyšný Kubín (Tupá skala and Ostrá skala), Žaškov, Jasenica, Mezibrodie, Oravský Podzámok and Sedliacka Dubová — mutually visible, with smoke signalling.

timeline.title: The demise of the hillfort at Dubová
timeline.description: A fire destroyed both the fortlet and the settlement below it in the Middle La Tène period; a demise simultaneous with that of the hillfort at Istebné is assumed, both probably captured and burnt down.

timeline.title: Slavic occupation of Ostrá skala
timeline.description: An occupation layer, a sunken dwelling with an oven and further settlement features with hearths on Ostrá skala above Vyšný Kubín; the Slavic fortification system made use of the older La Tène ramparts.

timeline.title: Occupation on the site of Orava Castle
timeline.description: Sherds of Slavic pottery and iron casting lumps discovered during the reconstruction of the main courtyard of today's Orava Castle.

timeline.title: Continuity of occupation on Ostrá skala
timeline.description: Demonstrated continuity between the two main chronological horizons of the use of the site, albeit at a lower intensity.

timeline.title: Later occupation of Ostrá skala
timeline.description: Dwellings of log construction; the hillfort at Vyšný Kubín survived until the 12th century, probably as an administrative seat even in the beginnings of the Hungarian state.

timeline.title: The incorporation of Orava into the Kingdom of Hungary
timeline.description: The Orava region became part of the early feudal Kingdom of Hungary; Orava Castle did not yet exist at that time.

children.text: Vyšný Kubín – Ostrá skala
One of the most thoroughly investigated sites in the Orava region –
Ostrá skala above Vyšný Kubín

– was occupied from the Eneolithic onwards. Its favourable position predestined it for the construction of a prehistoric fortified settlement. After building modifications, the site was secondarily reused in the Early Middle Ages. Ostrá skala was investigated archaeologically, with interruptions, from the beginning of the 1960s until the end of the 1970s.

The village of Vyšný Kubín (with an elevation of 525 m at its centre and of 490–1,612 m within its cadastral area) lies south-east of Dolný Kubín, on the north-western slope of the Choč mountains in the valley of the Leštiny stream. The site of Ostrá skala (812 m above sea level) is located on a rocky outcrop north of the village. In the early medieval period the focus of occupation fell into two horizons. From the turn of the 8th and 9th centuries come an occupation layer, a sunken dwelling with an oven and further settlement features with hearths. Among the finds, three spurs, scythes, bucket mounts, knives, axes, razors and weapons deserve mention. From the later phase, placed chronologically between the 10th century and the turn of the 12th and 13th centuries, dwellings of log construction were recognised in plan (charred remains of wooden beams). In the first chronological horizon the fortified settlement probably fulfilled a central administrative function in the region. On the basis of a long-running reassessment of the find situation (iron objects – weapons, horse equipment), continuity of occupation from the second half of the 9th century to the 10th century has now been demonstrated. This was the period between the two most important milestones in the early medieval use of the site. It does not, however, reach the intensity of the two dominant time spans.

blocks.alt: Slavic hillforts in the Orava region

children.text: The Slavic fortification system of the close of the 8th century and of the 9th century made use of the remains of fortifications from the preceding periods. It likewise built on an earlier arrangement of the interior of the hillfort, when a palisade enclosure divided the fortified settlement into three enclosures with an area of approximately 1.5–2 ha. The rampart, which in plan has the shape of an asymmetrical horseshoe, protected the highest settlement area, 2,500 m² in extent. The rampart originated in the La Tène period; the Slavs heightened it and set a wooden enclosure into it.

Bodies of regional administration were probably also concentrated at the hillfort. The Orava region was incorporated into the early feudal Kingdom of Hungary only at some point in the 11th century. Given that the hillfort at Vyšný Kubín survived until the 12th century, we assume that in some form it continued as an administrative seat even in the beginnings of the Hungarian state, since Orava Castle did not yet exist.

children.text: Dolný Kubín – Veľký Bysterec-Trniny

An upland site originally occupied in the Eneolithic, in the La Tène period and in the Early Roman period. On the basis of certain finds it is assumed that this site was used in the Early Middle Ages as well. Above all thanks to finds of gold and silver coins, the site was intensively dug over from the first half of the 19th century by many amateur researchers as well as by local inhabitants. A short trial excavation led by P. Čaplovič was carried out by the Orava Museum in 1957 and 1958. It was followed by further research work at the site, which took place at the end of the 1970s and in the 1980s.

blocks.alt: Slavic hillforts in the Orava region

children.text: Veľký Bysterec (with an elevation of 470 m at its centre and of 465–650 m within its cadastral area) is a district of the centre of lower Orava, that is, of Dolný Kubín. It lies in the south-western part of the Oravská vrchovina highlands. The site extends north-west of the town centre, on the upland position of Trniny. According to Hulínek, whether a Slavic fortified settlement stood here can so far be considered only in theoretical terms. This is inferred from two older finds (already known in the century before last) from Trniny, namely three-part mounts of Carolingian type. Further finds also come from the site (a small iron knife, or razor), dated to the early medieval period. The finds mentioned need not, however, be unambiguous proof of the existence of a fortified site whose beginnings would date as early as the close of the 8th century. Nor are early medieval building interventions in the fortification, which originally dated from the period of the Púchov culture, ruled out. This view is held by several archaeologists.
Istebné – Hrádok

The site of Hrádok at Istebné is formed by a naturally protected promontory above the Orava river, which was already occupied in prehistory. In the Hallstatt period a fortified settlement extended here. In the Early Middle Ages the area of Hrádok was occupied once again. Hrádok suffered badly from the construction of the railway in 1898, when a large part of the area of the hillfort was irretrievably destroyed. Research work was carried out in the undamaged parts of the site at the end of the 1950s and in the second half of the 1960s.

blocks.alt: Slavic hillforts in the Orava region

children.text: The lower Orava village of Istebné (with an elevation of 500 m at its centre and of 455–1,224 m within its cadastral area) lies where the spurs of the Malá Fatra and the Oravská vrchovina highlands meet (Pramene II 1992, 18, 19). The upland site of Hrádok, which yielded above all pottery finds of the 8th–9th and 10th–12th centuries, is located south of the village. The Slavic population made use of the earlier Hallstatt hillfort here. In the Early Middle Ages they set a Slavic palisade on the destruction layer of the older Hallstatt rampart.
Oravský Podzámok – Hrad (the Castle)

The dominant natural formation on which Orava Castle has stood since the 13th century was, together with its immediate surroundings, already occupied in prehistory. Finds of the Hallstatt period and of the period of the Púchov culture come from its surroundings. In the Early Middle Ages an upland settlement was probably located on this site.

The village of Oravský Podzámok (with an elevation of 520 m at its centre and of 495–1,224 m within its cadastral area) extends north of Dolný Kubín in the Oravská vrchovina highlands and at the same time on the southern slopes of the Oravská Magura. The settlement of the 9th century is located in the area (an upland position) where the castle, medieval in origin, stands today. During the general reconstruction of the castle, sherds of Slavic pottery, most probably of the 9th century, came to light in the main courtyard. Iron casting lumps, likewise found during the renovation in the main courtyard, may belong to the same chronological horizon. For this upland position we may consider a fortified settlement of the early medieval period as well, because of its favourable, strategic natural dispositions.

children.text: The Orava group

The Orava group, or the Orava type, was a local group of the Lusatian cultural complex in the northern basin of the Váh, the Orava and the Turiec, from c. 750 BC until 300 BC (although it flourished and is in fact relevantly attested only from 550 BC, that is, from Ha D2).

blocks.alt: Slavic hillforts in the Orava region

children.text: After 550 BC the territory of the Orava group was densely occupied, as is attested by a dense network of hillforts and of simple hamlets, as well as by cemeteries with a large number of graves. The most important hillforts of the Orava group were Tupá skala (above Vyšný Kubín) and Istebné – Hrádok. By then hillforts were also built with the help of stone, their inhabitants lived from crafts and sheep rearing, and they show signs of internal urbanisation. The Orava group is distinguished by specific pottery (the decoration consists of grooves; amphora-shaped and bulbous vessels predominate, together with S-profiled cups), by specific bronzes (diadems and neck rings made of a massive twisted or smooth rod and terminating in rosettes, ornate pins and so on) and by changes in the burial rite (more urnless cremation graves with the remains of the cremation placed in a small pit or covered with a sandstone slab). Sites with cremation cemeteries are, for example, Dolný Kubín, Vyšný Kubín and Oravský Podzámok. The Orava group was in close contact with the neighbouring territory of present-day Poland, as the form of the hillforts demonstrates.
The Hallstatt hillfort at Dubová

The Hallstatt period, as we call the Early Iron Age, is the period of prehistory from 700 to 400 BC. At that time the occupation of the Orava region was relatively dense. Fortified settlements are archaeologically attested, for example, at Tvrdošín, Podbiel, Istebné – Hrádok, Vyšný Kubín – Tupá skala and Ostrá skala, Žaškov – Hrádok, Jasenica – Hrdoš, Mezibrodie, Oravský Podzámok and Sedliacka Dubová – Žiar, and so are urn graves and unprotected settlements. All the fortified settlements have the character of an upland hillfort, that is to say, built on a hill, and they were erected in such places that one hillfort could be seen from another. A defensive system built in this way, making use of smoke signalling, formed a strong defensive unit of the local principality. The valleys of the Orava river and of its side tributaries provided agricultural land, but above all convenient crossings, and they made communication links with the main trade routes leading through Orava and Liptov possible. The importance of these routes is reflected by the hoards of bronzes from Komjatná, Žaškov, Osádka, Pucov, Istebné – Hrádok, Nižná and Krásna Hôrka.

children.text: The fortlet at Dubová is thus not an isolated feature. It was situated on the crown of a hill that cuts markedly into the valley of the Orava, through which an old trade route ran. The present remains of the fortified precinct of the little church at Dubová rest directly against the massive rampart of the Hallstatt hillfort. According to research so far, it was a feature with predominantly fortress-like characteristics.

The dominant element of the fortress was a neck rampart about 6 m high, which on the northern side separated the fortified hilltop from the rest of the ridge (the neck). The core of the rampart was a grillage-and-box construction of wooden roundwood filled with red burnt clay. The outer side of the rampart was provided with a supporting stone wall, which increased its defensive capacity. Its rear part sloped gently down into the enclosure. At the highest point of the rampart there was probably a wooden guardhouse – a watch post – from where the garrison had the best view of the approach road and of the whole surroundings. The earthen neck rampart as a whole gave the impression of a massive bastion, which was a key element in the fortification of the Hallstatt hillfort.

children.text: The rest of the fortification was secured by a wooden defensive gallery 4 metres wide, built on a stone footing 1 metre high. The gallery was probably faced on the outside with sandstone blocks and covered with a wooden roof. The places most accessible to the fortification were secured by a wedge-shaped ditch 2 metres deep. The entrance into the area of the fortress was secured by a gate tower and a bridge over the ditch.

As I have stated, the hillfort had above all a military purpose, and therefore the dwellings served mainly as quarters for the soldiers and for the captain of the fortress. The buildings in the enclosure were built at least 9 metres from the defensive gallery; sherds and daub were found in their original positions.

Below the fortified hilltop lay a hamlet, where the main economic life of the surrounding population took place. The settlement below the hillfort was situated on the site of the present village of Sedliacka Dubová, on the street leading from the municipal office to the cemetery, where the foundations of several Hallstatt farmsteads and sherds of Hallstatt character were uncovered, but where thickened rims of combed vessels already containing graphite from the Early La Tène period also appeared. The Hallstatt houses were built in terraced rows on the hillside of Žiar, because at that time the Orava river could still flood the valley.

We know very little about the history of the fortlet at Dubová; we can only date its demise to the Middle La Tène period, in the 3rd to 2nd century BC. The cause of its demise was a fire, which burnt down both the fortlet and the settlement below it. It is assumed that it came to an end together with the hillfort at Istebné. Both hillforts were probably captured and burnt down.

The theme of the Slavic hillforts in the Orava region is treated in detail in the extensive article by Drahoslav Hulínek and Michal Čajka: Včasnostredoveké hradiská na Orave v kontexte hradísk na Strednom a Západnom Slovensku (Early medieval hillforts in the Orava region in the context of the hillforts of Central and Western Slovakia), Slovenská archeológia LII-1, 2004. I have drawn most of the text from this very article.
